classification_rules.source_geometry: Supported only as a geometric observation when an exact candidate intersects source geometry by positive area; no administrative or legal resolution is implied.
classification_rules.physical_water_or_historic_course: Remain unresolved as a physical/legal classification. JRC GSW v1.5 and GLAD provide raster water-class observations at different temporal resolutions; GLAD is a separate classification product but uses Landsat sensors, and neither product locates exact banks, historic midstream positions, wetland/floodplain status, or legal effect.
classification_rules.processing_cause: Unresolved unless a specific processing step and mechanism are reproduced.
classification_rules.boundary_authority: Historical demarcation is partially evidenced by the 1928 Final Act and 1931 exchange of notes (official Treaty Series scan); candidate geometries east/south of terminal Beacon 47 remain unlocated relative to the treaty-defined river midstream. Present legal effect is not decided.

physical_water_or_historic_course.note: The original physical-gap diagnostic is unverified. Retained JRC GSW v1.5 pixels add evidence of surface-water occurrence within this candidate, including 2024 seasonality where present; exact present bank/course, waterbody type, historical course, floodplain/wetland status, and legal boundary remain unresolved. See jrc-gsw-water-analysis.json.

jrc_gsw_v1_5_observation.interpretation: Pixel-center counts from the unchanged candidate geometry; positive water-classified pixels are physical-reference observations, not an exact shoreline, historic channel, territorial assignment, or boundary-authority determination.

glad_global_surface_water_dynamics.grid: EPSG:4326; 0.00025 degree; approximately 30 m at equator
glad_global_surface_water_dynamics.tile_seam_aggregation: Each annual record merges disjoint tile pixel centers by year; counts are not duplicated across the 10E/20E tile seam.
glad_global_surface_water_dynamics.interpretation: Water-classified pixel centers in this product provide dated product evidence only. They do not locate exact bank/midstream lines, identify waterbody type, prove historical channel position, or resolve original diagnostic status.

processing_cause.finding: No exact data-processing defect or specific causal step has been reproduced.

boundary_authority.source: UK Treaty Series No. 28 (1931), Cmd. 3896; enclosed 1928 Final Act and beacon schedule
boundary_authority.finding: The original geometry bounds lie east and south of scheduled Beacon 47 at the Okavango/Cubango. The 1926 treaty defines a river-midstream segment beyond the beacon endpoint; no historical channel line is retained to locate this component against that rule.
boundary_authority.limits: This records a historical demarcation instrument and a coordinate comparison, not contemporary legal effect, territory, or an authoritative current line.

components.decision_limit: Positive-area overlap and slivers compare generalized administrative products; they do not identify which country is correct or whether candidate area is land/water.

boundary_authority.source: UK Treaty Series No. 28 (1931), Cmd. 3896; enclosed 1928 Final Act and beacon schedule

global_limits: Areas are planar EPSG:4326 square degrees; not ground-area estimates.
No geometry repair, clipping, snapping, reclassification, or territorial assignment was performed.
No present water edge, historic channel, demarcation monument, or exact legal boundary was independently located.
Source overlap is geometric product comparison only and cannot identify authority or processing cause.

The 1928 Final Act schedule provides 47 beacon records through Beacon 47 at the Okavango/Cubango; all 21 candidate bounds lie east/south of that endpoint. No historical channel or current midstream alignment east of Beacon 47 was reconstructed; do not use current or 30 m raster water classes as a substitute.

glad_surface_water_aggregate.annual_interval: 1999 through 2023; 25 unique years after tile-seam aggregation
glad_surface_water_aggregate.interpretation: Full annual and contact/pair results are retained in glad-water-1999-2023-analysis.json. Zero raster centers or no threshold detections do not establish dry ground.
